prompt: Which advantage of cloud computing lets a company replace large upfront data center purchases with payments only for the resources it actually consumes?

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense

explanation: Trading fixed expense for variable expense means paying only when you consume resources instead of investing in hardware before you know how you will use it. Going global in minutes is about deploying in multiple Regions quickly. Speed and agility is about how fast new resources become available to developers. Stopping guessing capacity is about scaling up and down instead of over- or under-provisioning; it is related, but it does not describe the change in how you pay.

prompt: A retailer's website traffic triples during a holiday sale and returns to normal a week later. Which cloud concept describes automatically adding and then removing resources to match this demand?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to acquire resources when you need them and release them when you do not, so capacity follows demand. Fault tolerance is about continuing to operate when a component fails, not about matching demand. Economies of scale explains why AWS prices are low, not how capacity changes. Agility is about how quickly teams can experiment and deliver, not about automatic scaling.

prompt: Why can AWS offer lower pay-as-you-go prices than most companies could achieve by running their own infrastructure?

options.text: Customers must commit to multi-year contracts
AWS does not charge for data transfer
Usage from a very large number of customers is aggregated, which creates economies of scale
Customers share servers without any isolation between them

explanation: Because usage from hundreds of thousands of customers is aggregated in the cloud, AWS achieves higher economies of scale, which translate into lower pay-as-you-go prices. Multi-year contracts are optional (for example Savings Plans), not required. AWS does charge for some data transfer, such as data sent out to the internet. Customers are isolated from each other; lack of isolation is not a source of savings.

prompt: A company wants to launch its application in several geographic Regions to serve customers worldwide, without building data centers there. Which advantage of cloud computing does this describe?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Trade fixed expense for variable expense

explanation: Going global in minutes means deploying an application in multiple Regions around the world with a few clicks, giving users lower latency at minimal cost. Economies of scale explain lower prices, not global reach. Not running data centers is about letting AWS handle the facilities. Trading fixed for variable expense is about how you pay, not where you deploy.

prompt: Developers at a company used to wait weeks for new test servers. On AWS they can create them in minutes and delete them when done. Which advantage of cloud computing does this describe?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale

explanation: Increased speed and agility means new IT resources are only a click away, so the time to make them available to developers drops from weeks to minutes. Economies of scale explain why prices are low. Stop guessing capacity is about matching capacity to demand. Going global in minutes is about deploying in many Regions.

prompt: A startup does not know how much traffic its new app will receive. It wants to avoid buying servers that sit idle or running out of capacity at launch. Which advantage of cloud computing helps most?

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense

explanation: Stop guessing capacity means you can scale up or down as needed instead of deciding infrastructure capacity before you know demand, which avoids both idle resources and shortages. Trading fixed for variable expense is about paying only for use, not about matching capacity to demand. Going global is about Regions. Speed and agility is about how quickly resources become available.

prompt: Which of the following are benefits of moving workloads to the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)

options.text: AWS takes over writing and maintaining the customer's application code
The ability to deploy applications in multiple Regions in minutes
The customer no longer has any security responsibilities
Paying only for the computing resources that are consumed
A guaranteed lower cost for every workload, regardless of how it is designed

explanation: Deploying globally in minutes and paying only for what you consume are core advantages of the AWS Cloud. AWS does not write or maintain customer application code. Under the shared responsibility model the customer always keeps security responsibilities, such as protecting its data and managing access. Costs depend on architecture and usage, so lower cost is not guaranteed for every workload.

prompt: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on a workload's ability to recover from failures and keep performing its intended function?
explanation: The reliability pillar covers a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, including recovering from failure. Performance efficiency is about using computing resources efficiently as demand and technology change. Operational excellence is about running and monitoring systems and continually improving processes. Sustainability is about minimizing the environmental impact of running workloads.

prompt: Which of the following are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
explanation: The six pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. Portability is not a pillar. Elasticity and scalability are cloud concepts that support several pillars (for example reliability and performance efficiency), but neither is a pillar itself.

prompt: A team replaces manual console changes with reviewed, version-controlled templates and scripts. Which Well-Architected pillar includes the design principle "perform operations as code"?
explanation: Performing operations as code is a design principle of the operational excellence pillar: you define the workload and its operations as code to limit human error and respond consistently to events. The security pillar focuses on protecting data and systems, cost optimization on avoiding unnecessary cost, and reliability on recovering from failure. Automation helps all of them, but this named principle belongs to operational excellence.

prompt: "Implement a strong identity foundation" is a design principle of which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
explanation: Implementing a strong identity foundation, such as least privilege and centralized identity management, is a design principle of the security pillar. Reliability covers recovering from failure. Operational excellence covers running and improving operations. Performance efficiency covers using resources efficiently.

prompt: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements and maintaining that efficiency as demand and technology change?
explanation: The performance efficiency pillar is about using computing resources efficiently to meet system requirements and keeping that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve. Cost optimization is about avoiding unnecessary costs. Reliability is about recovering from failure and meeting demand. Sustainability is about reducing environmental impact.

prompt: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads?
explanation: The sustainability pillar focuses on reducing the environmental impact of workloads, for example by maximizing utilization and choosing efficient services. Cost optimization often reduces waste too, but its focus is spending. Operational excellence is about running and improving systems. Performance efficiency is about meeting requirements with efficient resources.

prompt: "Automatically recover from failure" is a design principle of which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
explanation: The reliability pillar includes the design principle of monitoring key metrics and automatically triggering recovery when a threshold is breached. Security covers protecting data and systems. Cost optimization covers avoiding unnecessary cost. Sustainability covers reducing environmental impact.

prompt: A team wants to review its workload against AWS best practices, pillar by pillar, and track the improvements it plans to make. Which AWS service should the team use?
explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Tool lets you answer questions about a workload for each pillar, identifies high-risk issues, and tracks an improvement plan. AWS Config evaluates resource configurations against rules but does not review a workload's design. AWS Artifact provides compliance reports. Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities.

prompt: Which AWS resource organizes cloud adoption guidance into six perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, and Operations?
explanation: AWS CAF groups its guidance into six perspectives (Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, and Operations) to help organizations plan their cloud transformation. The Well-Architected Framework is organized into pillars and is used to review workload architecture. The shared responsibility model describes who secures what. AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs and gives no adoption guidance.

prompt: A company needs to move 60 TB of archived files to AWS from a remote site that has a slow, unreliable internet connection. Which option is the most appropriate?
explanation: Snowball Edge is a physical device that AWS ships to you, so large data sets can be moved without depending on the network. S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads but still sends every byte over the internet connection. AWS DMS migrates databases, not file archives. A Site-to-Site VPN encrypts traffic over the same slow internet link and adds no capacity.

prompt: Which perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) focuses on culture, organizational structure, leadership, and building the workforce's cloud skills?
explanation: The People perspective acts as a bridge between technology and business, covering culture, organizational structure, leadership, and workforce skills. Governance covers managing benefits and risks of the cloud initiative. Platform covers building the cloud platform and architecture. Operations covers delivering cloud services at agreed levels.

prompt: Which perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) helps ensure that cloud investments accelerate digital transformation and business outcomes?
explanation: The Business perspective helps ensure that cloud investments accelerate digital transformation ambitions and business outcomes. Security covers confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and workloads. Platform covers the cloud platform and architecture. Operations covers running cloud services to meet business needs.

prompt: A company moves an application from its data center to Amazon EC2 without changing the application. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Rehost, often called lift and shift, moves an application to the cloud without changes. Replatform makes a few cloud optimizations, such as moving to a managed database. Refactor re-architects the application to use cloud-native features. Retire decommissions applications that are no longer needed.

prompt: A company migrates its application to AWS and, along the way, moves its self-managed database to Amazon RDS without changing the application's core architecture. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Replatform, sometimes called lift, tinker, and shift, makes a few cloud optimizations, such as adopting a managed database, without changing the core architecture. Rehost moves the application unchanged. Repurchase replaces the application with a different product, often SaaS. Retain keeps the application where it is for now.

prompt: A company decides to stop running its own customer relationship management (CRM) software and to use a software as a service (SaaS) CRM product instead. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Repurchase, also called drop and shop, replaces an application with a different product, typically SaaS. Refactor re-architects the existing application. Relocate moves infrastructure, such as VMware workloads, to the cloud without changes. Rehost moves the existing application unchanged.

prompt: Which AWS services help move existing data or databases to AWS? (Choose two.)
explanation: AWS DMS migrates databases to AWS with minimal downtime, and Snowball Edge physically transfers large amounts of data. Amazon Lex builds chatbots. AWS Artifact provides compliance reports. Amazon QuickSight builds business intelligence dashboards.

prompt: Which statement best describes rightsizing?

options.text: Buying the largest available instance type so the workload never runs out of capacity
Moving every workload to Reserved Instances
Combining accounts under one organization to receive volume discounts
Matching instance types and sizes to a workload's performance and capacity needs at the lowest possible cost

explanation: Rightsizing is the process of matching instance types and sizes to workload performance and capacity requirements at the lowest possible cost. Buying the largest instance is over-provisioning, the opposite of rightsizing. Reserved Instances are a pricing commitment and do not change whether the size fits the workload. Consolidating accounts is about billing, not resource sizing.

prompt: A company moves its workloads from its own data center to AWS. Which costs does the company no longer pay for directly? (Choose two.)

options.text: Power, cooling, and floor space for server rooms
Salaries of the developers who build its applications
Licenses for software it brings under a Bring Your Own License model
The effort of classifying and protecting its own data

explanation: In the cloud, the company stops paying to run and maintain data center facilities and stops making upfront hardware purchases; those become part of the variable price of AWS services. Application developers are still needed. With Bring Your Own License, the company keeps paying for its own licenses. Classifying and protecting its data remains the customer's responsibility.

prompt: A company wants to use the Microsoft software licenses it already owns when it moves its servers to AWS. Which licensing approach is this called?
explanation: Bring Your Own License (BYOL) means using licenses you already own on AWS, subject to the vendor's terms; AWS License Manager helps track them. License included means the license cost is part of the AWS price. Savings Plans and Reserved Instances are compute pricing commitments, not licensing models.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a variable cost?

options.text: Buying servers for a new data center
Signing a three-year lease for data center space
Paying for Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances only for the time they run
Paying an annual hardware maintenance contract

explanation: A variable cost changes with usage; On-Demand Instances are billed only for the time they run. Buying servers, leasing data center space, and annual maintenance contracts are fixed costs that you pay whether or not the capacity is used.

prompt: How does using AWS CloudFormation to provision infrastructure help reduce costs?

options.text: CloudFormation makes every resource it creates free of charge
It automates repeatable provisioning, which reduces manual effort and configuration errors
It automatically moves workloads to the cheapest Region
It applies Reserved Instance discounts to every stack

explanation: CloudFormation provisions resources from templates in a consistent, repeatable way, which saves engineering time and avoids costly mistakes from manual setup. The resources it creates are billed normally. It does not choose Regions for you or apply pricing discounts.

prompt: A company wants a relational database without having to install, patch, or back up the database software itself. Which option should it choose?

options.text: MySQL installed on an Amazon EC2 instance

explanation: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service: AWS handles tasks such as software patching and automated backups. Running MySQL on EC2 leaves installation, patching, and backups to the customer. Amazon EBS is block storage, not a database. An on-premises server leaves all of that work with the company.

prompt: Which AWS service analyzes resource utilization and recommends better-sized Amazon EC2 instances to reduce cost or improve performance?
explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer uses utilization metrics to recommend optimal instance types and sizes, which supports rightsizing. AWS Budgets alerts on spending against thresholds. AWS Artifact provides compliance reports. Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities.

prompt: Which statements describe the AWS pay-as-you-go pricing model? (Choose two.)

options.text: There is no upfront commitment required
Prices are fixed for a three-year term
Customers pay only for the resources they use
A minimum monthly spend is required
Customers must purchase hardware before using services

explanation: With pay-as-you-go pricing you pay only for what you use, with no long-term contract or upfront commitment required. Fixed multi-year terms exist only if you choose commitments such as Savings Plans. There is no minimum monthly spend, and no hardware purchase.

prompt: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task is AWS responsible for?

options.text: Patching the guest operating system on Amazon EC2 instances
Physically securing the data centers that run AWS services

explanation: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, which includes the facilities, hardware, and networking that run AWS services. Security group rules, guest operating system patches on EC2, and IAM permissions are all security in the cloud, which the customer configures and manages.

prompt: A company runs a database on Amazon RDS. Which task remains the company's responsibility?

options.text: Replacing failed disks in the database host
Controlling which users and network sources can connect to the database
Patching the operating system of the database host
Maintaining the physical network inside the Availability Zone

explanation: With a managed service such as Amazon RDS, the customer still controls access: security groups, IAM permissions, and database users. AWS replaces failed hardware, patches the host operating system, and maintains the physical network, which is why responsibilities shift toward AWS as services become more managed.

prompt: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. Which tasks are the company's responsibility under the shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)

options.text: Installing security patches on the guest operating system
Destroying storage hardware at the end of its life
Securing the network cabling between data centers

explanation: For EC2, the customer manages the guest operating system (including patches) and is responsible for protecting its own data, including encryption choices. The hypervisor, the disposal of storage hardware, and the physical network between data centers are part of the infrastructure that AWS secures.

prompt: A company runs code on AWS Lambda. Which task is the company's responsibility?

options.text: Patching the operating system of the servers that run the functions
Writing the function code and setting its IAM permissions
Adding servers when the number of requests grows
Maintaining the physical hardware in the data center

explanation: With Lambda, AWS manages the servers, operating system, and scaling; the customer is responsible for its function code, its configuration, and the permissions it uses. Patching the underlying operating system, scaling the server fleet, and maintaining hardware are AWS responsibilities for this serverless service.

prompt: Which task is the customer's responsibility when storing data in Amazon S3?

options.text: Replacing failed disks in the storage hardware
Maintaining the durability of the underlying storage infrastructure
Configuring bucket policies and access to the stored objects
Maintaining the network inside the AWS Region

explanation: The customer decides who can access its S3 data, through bucket policies, access control, and Block Public Access settings. Replacing hardware, providing the durability of the underlying infrastructure, and running the network are AWS responsibilities.

prompt: Which of the following is a shared control, where AWS and the customer each have a part of the responsibility?

options.text: Physical and environmental security of data centers
Deciding which data the customer stores and how it is classified
Security of the edge locations' facilities

explanation: Patch management is a shared control: AWS patches the infrastructure, while customers patch their guest operating systems and applications. Physical and environmental security, including edge location facilities, is entirely AWS's responsibility. Choosing and classifying data is entirely the customer's responsibility.

prompt: Which tasks are AWS responsibilities under the shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configuring security groups for the customer's instances
Securing the hardware that runs AWS services
Maintaining the AWS global network infrastructure
Creating and managing the customer's IAM users

explanation: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, which includes the hardware and the global network infrastructure that run AWS services. Configuring security groups, deciding how to encrypt data, and managing IAM users are customer responsibilities: security in the cloud.

prompt: As a customer moves a workload from Amazon EC2 to more managed services such as Amazon RDS or Amazon DynamoDB, how does the customer's share of security responsibility generally change?

options.text: It decreases, because AWS operates more of the stack

explanation: The more managed the service, the more of the stack AWS operates, such as the operating system and database software, so the customer's responsibilities shrink. They never disappear: the customer still controls data, access, and configuration. That rules out "increases", "stays the same", and "moves entirely to AWS".

prompt: An auditor asks a company for AWS's SOC reports and ISO certifications. Which service provides on-demand access to these documents?
explanation: AWS Artifact provides on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance documents such as SOC reports and ISO certifications. AWS Config records and evaluates the configuration of your own resources. Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations for your account. Audit Manager helps collect evidence about your own usage for audits; it is not where AWS's own reports are downloaded.

prompt: A security team needs to find out which user deleted an Amazon S3 bucket and when. Which service records this kind of account activity?
explanation: CloudTrail records actions taken by users, roles, and AWS services as events, including who made the request and when. CloudWatch collects metrics and logs for monitoring performance. GuardDuty analyzes activity to detect threats but is not the audit record itself. AWS Config tracks how resource configurations change over time, not who called which API.

prompt: Which service continuously analyzes sources such as AWS CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs to detect potentially malicious activity in an AWS account?
explanation: GuardDuty is a threat detection service that monitors and analyzes data sources such as CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs. Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks. Macie discovers and helps protect sensitive data stored in Amazon S3.

prompt: Which AWS service records how resource configurations change over time and evaluates them against rules, such as "S3 buckets must not be public"?
explanation: AWS Config records resource configurations and their history, and evaluates them against rules to show compliance. AWS CloudTrail records API activity: who did what. Amazon CloudWatch collects metrics and logs. AWS Artifact provides AWS compliance reports.

prompt: Which AWS service automatically scans Amazon EC2 instances, container images, and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure?
explanation: Amazon Inspector continuously scans workloads for known software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. GuardDuty detects threats from activity such as unusual API calls. Macie finds sensitive data in S3. Shield protects against DDoS attacks.

prompt: Which AWS service protects applications against distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, with a Standard tier that is included at no additional cost?
explanation: AWS Shield provides DDoS protection; Shield Standard is automatically included at no extra cost, and Shield Advanced adds more protection. AWS WAF filters web requests, such as SQL injection attempts. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities. GuardDuty detects threats from activity in the account.

prompt: A company wants one place that collects security findings from several AWS security services and checks its accounts against best-practice standards. Which service meets this need?
explanation: AWS Security Hub aggregates findings from services such as GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie and runs automated checks against security standards. Trusted Advisor gives recommendations across several categories but is not a findings aggregator. AWS Config evaluates resource configurations. CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs.

prompt: Which AWS service creates and controls the cryptographic keys used to encrypt data at rest in many AWS services?
explanation: AWS KMS creates and manages cryptographic keys and integrates with many services to encrypt data at rest. Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets such as passwords. ACM provides TLS certificates for encryption in transit. IAM controls who can access resources.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of encryption in transit?

options.text: Encrypting objects stored in Amazon S3 with server-side encryption
Using HTTPS (TLS) between a user's browser and a load balancer
Using an encrypted Amazon EBS volume
Rotating an AWS KMS key every year

explanation: Encryption in transit protects data while it moves across a network, which is what HTTPS (TLS) does. Server-side encryption in S3 and encrypted EBS volumes protect data at rest. Key rotation is a key management practice, not a type of encryption in transit.

prompt: Which AWS service uses machine learning to discover and help protect sensitive data, such as personally identifiable information, stored in Amazon S3?
explanation: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data such as personally identifiable information in S3 buckets and reports on bucket security. Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities. GuardDuty detects threats from account activity. AWS Config tracks resource configurations.

prompt: A company preparing for an audit wants to continuously collect evidence about how it uses AWS and map it to a compliance framework. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Audit Manager continuously collects evidence from your AWS usage and organizes it against frameworks to simplify audits. AWS Artifact provides AWS's own compliance reports, not evidence about your usage. CloudTrail records API activity, which can be one source of evidence. Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations.

prompt: Which AWS services help a company monitor and audit governance in its AWS account? (Choose two.)
explanation: AWS CloudTrail records who made which API call and when, and AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations; both support auditing and governance. Amazon Lex builds chatbots, Snowball Edge transfers data physically, and Amazon Polly converts text to speech.

prompt: Which practice is recommended for protecting the AWS account root user?

options.text: Create root user access keys for automation scripts
Share the root user password among the administrators
Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) and avoid using the root user for everyday tasks
Delete the root user after creating an administrator

explanation: AWS recommends enabling MFA on the root user and using it only for the few tasks that require it. Root user access keys should not be created because they grant unrestricted access. Root credentials should never be shared. The root user cannot be deleted; it exists for the life of the account.

prompt: An application running on an Amazon EC2 instance needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to give the application permission?

options.text: Attach an IAM role with the required permissions to the instance
Store an IAM user's access keys in the application code
Save access keys in a configuration file on the instance
Use the root user's access keys

explanation: An IAM role attached to the instance provides temporary credentials that are rotated automatically, so no long-term keys are stored. Access keys in code or in a file on the instance are long-term credentials that can leak and must be rotated by hand. Root user access keys grant unrestricted access and should never be used by applications.

prompt: Which tasks can only be performed by the AWS account root user? (Choose two.)

options.text: Changing the account name or the root user email address
Restoring the permissions of the only IAM administrator after that administrator removed their own permissions

explanation: Changing account settings such as the account name and root user email address, and restoring IAM user permissions when the only administrator has revoked their own, are on the list of tasks that require root user credentials. Creating IAM users, launching EC2 instances, and creating S3 buckets can all be done by IAM identities with the right permissions.

prompt: Granting each user only the permissions needed to do their job, and nothing more, is an example of which security principle?
explanation: The principle of least privilege means granting only the permissions required to perform a task. Multi-factor authentication adds a second sign-in factor. Federation lets users sign in with an external identity provider. Defense in depth means applying security at multiple layers.

prompt: Twenty developers need the same set of AWS permissions. What is the simplest way to manage this with IAM users?

options.text: Attach the same inline policy to each user separately
Create an IAM group, attach the policy to the group, and add the users to it
Let all developers share one IAM user's credentials
Give each developer the root user's credentials

explanation: IAM groups let you attach permissions once and manage membership, so every user in the group gets the same permissions. Separate inline policies are hard to keep consistent. Shared credentials remove accountability. The root user should never be shared or used for daily work.

prompt: A company wants its employees to sign in once and access multiple AWS accounts and business applications, using its existing corporate directory. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS Single Sign-On) gives workforce users single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts and applications and can connect to an existing identity source. Amazon Cognito handles sign-in for users of your own applications. AWS Organizations manages accounts but does not provide sign-on. Access keys are long-term credentials for programmatic access.

prompt: An application needs a database password. The company wants to store it securely and rotate it automatically. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets such as database credentials and can rotate them automatically. AWS KMS manages encryption keys, not application secrets. ACM manages TLS certificates. Storing passwords in S3 would require building protection and rotation yourself.

prompt: What is an AWS managed policy in IAM?

options.text: A policy embedded directly in a single IAM user, group, or role
A standalone policy that AWS creates and maintains
A standalone policy that the customer writes and maintains in its own account
A policy that sets the maximum permissions for accounts in an organization

explanation: AWS managed policies are standalone policies created and administered by AWS for common use cases. A policy embedded in one identity is an inline policy. A policy you write and maintain is a customer managed policy. Maximum permissions for accounts in an organization are set with service control policies (SCPs).

prompt: Which feature adds a second step to signing in, such as a code from an authenticator app, in addition to a password?
explanation: MFA requires a second factor, such as a code from an authenticator app or a security key, in addition to the password. A password policy sets rules for passwords but adds no second factor. Access keys are credentials for programmatic access. An IAM role provides temporary permissions.

prompt: A company wants every IAM user password to have a minimum length and to include symbols. Which IAM feature enforces this?
explanation: An IAM account password policy sets requirements such as minimum length, character types, and expiration for IAM user passwords. SCPs limit permissions across accounts in an organization. MFA adds a second sign-in factor. IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources shared outside your account.

prompt: Which approaches give people or workloads access to AWS without creating long-term IAM user credentials for them? (Choose two.)

options.text: Federating users from an external identity provider into IAM roles
Embedding access keys in application code
Using AWS IAM Identity Center for workforce sign-in
Creating one IAM user that the whole team shares

explanation: Federation into IAM roles and IAM Identity Center both provide temporary credentials, so no long-term user credentials are created. Sharing root credentials, embedding access keys, and sharing one IAM user all rely on long-term credentials and remove accountability.

prompt: Which statement about security groups is correct?

options.text: They are stateless and are evaluated at the subnet level
They inspect web requests to block SQL injection attacks
They absorb distributed denial of service (DDoS) traffic at edge locations
They are stateful and control traffic for the resources they are attached to, such as EC2 instances

explanation: A security group is a stateful virtual firewall for the resources it is associated with, such as EC2 instances: return traffic for an allowed request is automatically allowed. Stateless rules evaluated at the subnet level describe network ACLs. Inspecting web requests for attacks such as SQL injection is AWS WAF. Absorbing DDoS traffic is AWS Shield.

prompt: Which VPC feature is stateless, applies at the subnet level, and supports both allow and deny rules?
explanation: Network ACLs are stateless, are associated with subnets, and can contain allow and deny rules. Security groups are stateful, apply to resources such as instances, and support only allow rules. AWS WAF filters web requests. AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks.

prompt: A company wants to block SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts in requests to its website behind Amazon CloudFront. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that inspects HTTP requests and can block common attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Shield protects against DDoS. Security groups filter traffic by port and source, not by request content. Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities.

prompt: Where can a company find and buy third-party security software, such as firewalls and endpoint protection, that runs on AWS?
explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated catalog where customers find, buy, and deploy third-party software, including security products. AWS Artifact provides compliance reports. Security Hub aggregates security findings. Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations.

prompt: Which AWS resource publishes articles about security best practices, new security features, and how customers solve security problems on AWS?
explanation: The AWS Security Blog publishes posts about AWS security services, features, and best practices. AWS Artifact offers compliance reports, not articles. Cost Explorer and the Pricing Calculator are cost tools.

prompt: Which AWS service checks an account for issues such as security groups that allow unrestricted access and a root user without MFA, as part of its recommendations?
explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor runs checks across categories including security, for example flagging unrestricted security group rules and the root user's MFA status. Macie finds sensitive data in S3. AWS Artifact provides compliance reports. CloudTrail records API activity.

prompt: By default, what traffic does a newly created security group allow?

options.text: All inbound and all outbound traffic
No inbound traffic and all outbound traffic
No inbound and no outbound traffic
All inbound traffic and no outbound traffic

explanation: A new security group has no inbound rules, so inbound traffic is denied until you add rules, and it has an outbound rule that allows all outbound traffic. The other combinations do not match the default behavior.

prompt: Which features can control network traffic to and from Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC? (Choose two.)
explanation: Security groups filter traffic for the instances they are attached to, and network ACLs filter traffic for whole subnets. An IAM password policy governs sign-in passwords. AWS Artifact provides compliance reports. Macie finds sensitive data in S3.

prompt: A team wants to create the same set of AWS resources repeatedly in several accounts by using version-controlled templates. Which service should the team use?
explanation: CloudFormation is infrastructure as code: you describe resources in a template and CloudFormation provisions them the same way every time. The Management Console is for manual, one-time operations. CloudShell is a browser-based shell for running commands; it does not model resources as templates. The Health Dashboard reports events that affect AWS services and your resources.

prompt: A company needs a dedicated, private network connection between its data center and AWS that does not use the public internet. Which service meets this requirement?
explanation: Direct Connect links your network to AWS over a dedicated connection that bypasses the public internet. A Site-to-Site VPN is encrypted but travels over the internet. An internet gateway connects a VPC to the internet. CloudFront is a content delivery network for serving content to users, not a private link to a data center.

prompt: Which AWS tool lets a user run AWS CLI commands from the browser, already authenticated, without installing anything locally?
explanation: AWS CloudShell is a browser-based shell, launched from the console, with the AWS CLI preinstalled and the user's credentials already available. CodeBuild compiles and tests code in build projects. Systems Manager manages fleets of servers. AWS Marketplace is a software catalog.

prompt: A company keeps some workloads in its own data center and runs others on AWS, connected to each other. Which deployment model is this?
explanation: A hybrid deployment connects cloud resources with existing on-premises infrastructure. A cloud deployment runs everything in the cloud. An on-premises (private cloud) deployment keeps everything in the company's own data centers. Multi-Region describes spreading a workload across AWS Regions, not a deployment model.

prompt: A developer wants a Python application to upload files to Amazon S3 programmatically. What should the developer use?

options.text: An AWS SDK, such as the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3)

explanation: AWS SDKs give applications programmatic access to AWS services in their own language; Boto3 is the SDK for Python. The Management Console is a web interface for people. AWS Marketplace is a software catalog. The Health Dashboard reports service events.

prompt: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between AWS Regions and Availability Zones?

options.text: Each Availability Zone contains multiple Regions
Each Region contains multiple isolated Availability Zones
An Availability Zone is another name for an edge location
Availability Zones are shared between neighboring Regions

explanation: A Region is a separate geographic area that contains multiple isolated locations called Availability Zones. An Availability Zone belongs to exactly one Region, so it cannot contain Regions or be shared between them. Edge locations are separate sites used by services such as CloudFront to serve content close to users.

prompt: Which of the following are valid reasons to deploy a workload in more than one AWS Region? (Choose two.)

options.text: To recover from a disaster that affects an entire Region
To increase the number of IAM users the account can have
To avoid having to use Availability Zones
To reduce latency for users in a distant geographic area
To remove all data transfer charges

explanation: Multiple Regions support disaster recovery and business continuity, and placing resources closer to distant users lowers latency. IAM is a global service, so adding Regions does not change IAM limits. Each Region still uses Availability Zones for high availability. Transferring data between Regions is charged, so multi-Region designs add data transfer cost.

prompt: Amazon CloudFront caches content in which part of the AWS global infrastructure to reduce latency for users?
explanation: Edge locations are sites in many cities worldwide where CloudFront caches content close to users. Availability Zones and Regions host resources such as EC2 instances. VPC subnets are network segments inside a VPC.

prompt: A company wants its web application to stay available if one data center in a Region fails. What should it do?

options.text: Run the application on a larger EC2 instance
Run instances in multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer
Serve the application from multiple edge locations only
Add more instances in the same Availability Zone

explanation: Availability Zones are isolated from each other's failures, so running in more than one AZ keeps the application available if one fails. A larger instance or more instances in one AZ still share that AZ's failure. Edge locations cache content but do not run the application's servers.

prompt: Which AWS offering places compute and storage inside telecommunications providers' 5G networks to give mobile devices ultra-low latency?
explanation: AWS Wavelength embeds AWS compute and storage in 5G networks so applications reach mobile devices with single-digit millisecond latency. Local Zones place AWS infrastructure near large metropolitan areas. Outposts run AWS infrastructure in your own data center. CloudFront is a content delivery network.

prompt: A regulation requires a company's customer data to stay within one country. How can the company meet this on AWS?

options.text: Store the data in an AWS Region located in that country
Store the data in edge locations in that country
Spread the data across Availability Zones in any Region

explanation: Data you store in a Region stays in that Region unless you move it, so choosing a Region in the required country supports data residency. Edge locations cache content and are not where you store primary data. Global Accelerator routes traffic. Availability Zones are inside a Region, so their country depends on the Region chosen.

prompt: A developer wants to run code in response to file uploads without provisioning or managing servers, paying only for the compute time used. Which service is the best fit?
explanation: Lambda runs code in response to events without servers to provision or manage, and you pay for the compute time consumed. EC2 and Lightsail provide virtual servers that you manage and pay for while they run. Elastic Beanstalk automates deployment but still runs your application on EC2 instances in your account.

prompt: A team wants to run containers on Amazon ECS without managing the underlying servers. Which option should the team choose?
explanation: Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers, so you do not provision or manage EC2 instances for your tasks. Amazon ECR stores container images; it does not run them. EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the number of EC2 instances, which you would still manage. Dedicated Hosts are physical servers reserved for your use, the opposite of not managing servers.

prompt: Which Amazon EC2 instance family is best suited for compute-bound workloads, such as batch processing and high-performance web servers?
explanation: Compute optimized instances have high-performance processors for compute-bound applications such as batch processing and web servers. Memory optimized instances suit large in-memory data sets. Storage optimized instances suit high, sequential read and write access to local storage. Accelerated computing instances use hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

prompt: A company runs an in-memory database that processes very large data sets. Which Amazon EC2 instance family fits best?
explanation: Memory optimized instances deliver fast performance for workloads that process large data sets in memory. Compute optimized instances favor processor power. Storage optimized instances favor fast local disk access. General purpose instances balance resources without favoring memory.

prompt: Which service automatically adds Amazon EC2 instances when demand rises and removes them when demand falls?
explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the number of instances to match demand, which provides elasticity. Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic across instances but does not add or remove them. CloudWatch provides the metrics and alarms that scaling can use. Lightsail offers simple virtual private servers.

prompt: Which service distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, in multiple Availability Zones?
explanation: Elastic Load Balancing spreads incoming traffic across healthy targets in one or more Availability Zones. Auto Scaling changes the number of instances. API Gateway creates and manages APIs. CloudFront delivers cached content from edge locations.

prompt: Which AWS compute options are serverless, meaning the customer does not provision or manage servers? (Choose two.)
explanation: AWS Lambda runs code without servers to manage, and AWS Fargate runs containers without managing the underlying instances. EC2 instances, Dedicated Hosts, and Lightsail instances are servers that the customer provisions and manages.

prompt: Which service is a fully managed NoSQL key-value and document database?
explanation: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database that supports key-value and document data models. Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora are relational database services. Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics on structured data using SQL.

prompt: Which AWS database is a MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database built for the cloud?
explanation: Amazon Aurora is a fully managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, built for the cloud. DynamoDB is a NoSQL database. Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics. ElastiCache is an in-memory cache.

prompt: A company wants to reduce load on its database by caching frequent query results in memory. Which service fits best?
explanation: Amazon ElastiCache is a managed in-memory cache (compatible with Valkey, Redis OSS, and Memcached) that speeds up applications and offloads databases. RDS is a relational database, not a cache. Redshift is a data warehouse. S3 Glacier is archival storage.

prompt: When would a company choose to run its database on Amazon EC2 instead of using Amazon RDS?

options.text: When it wants AWS to handle backups and patching
When it needs full control of the operating system or a database engine that RDS does not offer
When it wants the least operational effort
When it wants automatic Multi-AZ failover managed by AWS

explanation: Self-managing a database on EC2 makes sense when you need operating-system access or an engine or configuration that RDS does not support. Managed backups and patching, low operational effort, and managed Multi-AZ failover are reasons to choose RDS instead.

prompt: A company is moving from an Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and needs to convert its database schema and code to the new engine. Which tool helps with this?
explanation: AWS SCT converts database schemas and code from one engine to another, and is often used together with AWS DMS for heterogeneous migrations. Athena queries data in S3. AWS Backup centralizes backups. Redshift is a data warehouse.

prompt: A company wants to register a domain name and route users to its application by using DNS. Which service provides both capabilities?
explanation: Route 53 is a DNS web service that provides domain registration, DNS routing, and health checking. CloudFront delivers content through edge locations but does not register domains or act as your DNS service. Direct Connect is a dedicated network link to AWS. Amazon VPC is an isolated virtual network for your resources.

prompt: What makes a subnet in a VPC a public subnet?

options.text: It has a route to an internet gateway
It has a route to a NAT gateway only
It is located in an edge location

explanation: A public subnet has a route in its route table to an internet gateway, so resources with public IP addresses can reach the internet directly. A route only to a NAT gateway is typical of a private subnet. Every subnet is associated with a route table. Subnets are in Availability Zones, not edge locations.

prompt: Instances in a private subnet need to download software updates from the internet but must not accept connections started from the internet. What should be used?

options.text: An internet gateway route in the private subnet

explanation: A NAT gateway lets instances in private subnets start outbound connections to the internet while blocking connections initiated from the internet. Routing the subnet to an internet gateway would make it public. Direct Connect links a data center to AWS. Route 53 is a DNS service.

prompt: A company has users worldwide and wants to improve the availability and performance of a non-cacheable TCP application by routing traffic over the AWS global network through static IP addresses. Which service fits best?
explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes traffic over the AWS global network to healthy endpoints, which suits TCP and UDP applications. CloudFront mainly caches and delivers content. Route 53 answers DNS queries but does not carry traffic. Direct Connect links on-premises networks to AWS.

prompt: Which AWS services connect an on-premises network to a VPC? (Choose two.)
explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted connection over the internet, and AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private connection; both link on-premises networks to a VPC. CloudFront delivers content to users. Route 53 is a DNS service. Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic to targets.

prompt: A company must keep compliance records for 10 years. The records are almost never read, and waiting up to 12 hours to retrieve them is acceptable. Which Amazon S3 storage class has the lowest storage cost for this data?

options.text: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)

explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class and is designed for long-term data that is rarely accessed, with retrieval within hours. S3 Standard is for frequently accessed data and costs the most to store. S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA offer millisecond access for infrequently used data, at a higher storage price than the archive classes.

prompt: Which services provide managed file systems that many compute instances can mount at the same time by using standard file protocols such as NFS or SMB? (Choose two.)
explanation: Amazon EFS provides shared NFS file systems, and Amazon FSx provides managed file systems such as FSx for Windows File Server (SMB). Amazon EBS provides block storage volumes attached to instances rather than a shared file service. Instance store is temporary block storage physically attached to the host. DynamoDB is a NoSQL database, not a file system.

prompt: Which storage option provides durable block-level volumes that attach to an EC2 instance and keep their data when the instance stops?
explanation: Amazon EBS volumes are durable block storage that persist independently of the instance's life. Instance store is temporary block storage whose data is lost when the instance stops or terminates. S3 is object storage. EFS is a shared file system.

prompt: A company wants objects in Amazon S3 to move automatically to a cheaper storage class 30 days after they are created. What should it configure?
explanation: S3 Lifecycle rules transition objects to other storage classes, or expire them, after a set time. Versioning keeps multiple versions of objects. Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads over long distances. Cross-Region Replication copies objects to another Region.

prompt: On-premises applications need to keep using file shares while the data is stored in AWS, with frequently used data cached locally. Which service fits best?
explanation: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications to cloud storage and keeps a local cache for low-latency access to frequently used data. Snowball Edge is a device for physical data transfer. EFS is a file system for AWS compute, not a local cache. AWS Backup centralizes backups.

prompt: Which AWS service helps data scientists build, train, and deploy machine learning models?
explanation: Amazon SageMaker provides tools to build, train, and deploy machine learning models. Amazon Lex builds conversational interfaces. Amazon Kendra is intelligent enterprise search. Amazon QuickSight builds business intelligence dashboards.

prompt: A company wants to add a chatbot that understands both voice and text to its customer service app. Which AWS service should it use?
explanation: Amazon Lex builds conversational interfaces (chatbots) that understand voice and text. Amazon Polly turns text into speech but does not understand conversations. Amazon Kendra searches documents. Amazon Athena queries data in S3 with SQL.

prompt: Employees need to search across thousands of internal documents by asking questions in natural language. Which AWS service is designed for this?
explanation: Amazon Kendra is an intelligent search service that finds answers in enterprise documents from natural language questions. Lex builds chatbots. Athena runs SQL queries on data in S3. QuickSight builds dashboards.

prompt: Which service lets analysts query data stored in Amazon S3 using standard SQL, without setting up or managing servers?
explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service for analyzing data in S3 with SQL, paying per query. Kinesis collects and processes streaming data. QuickSight visualizes data in dashboards. AWS Glue prepares and transforms data (ETL) and catalogs it.

prompt: A company wants to clean and transform raw data, then show the results to managers in interactive dashboards. Which AWS services should it use? (Choose two.)
explanation: AWS Glue prepares and transforms data (extract, transform, and load), and Amazon QuickSight builds interactive business intelligence dashboards. Amazon Lex builds chatbots, Amazon Connect runs contact centers, and Amazon Kendra provides document search.

prompt: An order system must decouple its web tier from its processing tier, so that messages wait in a queue until a worker processes them. Which service fits best?
explanation: Amazon SQS is a message queue: messages are stored until a consumer retrieves and processes them, which decouples components. SNS pushes messages to subscribers (publish/subscribe) rather than holding them for a worker. SES sends email. EventBridge routes events between applications using rules.

prompt: When a server fails, a company wants to notify its on-call team by email and SMS at the same time. Which service should send these notifications?
explanation: Amazon SNS publishes a message to a topic and delivers it to all subscribers, including email addresses and phone numbers (SMS). SQS stores messages for applications to poll. SES sends email only. Amazon Connect is a contact center service.

prompt: Which AWS service provides a cloud-based contact center for customer service agents?
explanation: Amazon Connect is an omnichannel cloud contact center. SES sends email. Lex builds chatbots, which can be used inside Connect but is not a contact center itself. WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops.

prompt: Remote employees need full, persistent Windows or Linux desktops that they can reach from any device. Which AWS service fits best?
explanation: Amazon WorkSpaces provides persistent virtual desktops that users reach from many devices. AppStream 2.0 streams individual applications rather than a full desktop. Amplify builds web and mobile apps. Lightsail offers simple virtual servers.

prompt: A small team wants to build and host a full-stack web application quickly, with hosting and a backend handled for them. Which AWS service is designed for this?
explanation: AWS Amplify provides tools and hosting to build and deploy full-stack web and mobile apps quickly. AppSync creates GraphQL APIs, which can be one part of a backend. WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops. IoT Core connects IoT devices.

prompt: A manufacturer wants to securely connect thousands of sensors to the cloud and route their messages to other AWS services. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS IoT Core connects IoT devices to the cloud securely and routes their messages to other services. IoT Greengrass runs software on edge devices themselves. SQS is a message queue for applications, not a device gateway. Kendra is document search.

prompt: A company runs a nightly batch job that can be stopped and restarted at any time without losing work. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option offers the lowest cost for this workload?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at a steep discount compared with On-Demand prices, in exchange for the chance of interruption, which suits a fault-tolerant batch job. On-Demand Instances cost more and are meant for workloads that cannot be interrupted. Dedicated Hosts are physical servers for licensing or compliance needs and are the most expensive option. Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity at On-Demand rates and give no discount.

prompt: A company has steady compute usage and wants a discount for a 3-year commitment. It expects to change instance families and Regions, and to move some workloads to AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda. Which option fits best?
explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 usage regardless of instance family, size, or Region, and also apply to Fargate and Lambda usage, in exchange for a 1- or 3-year commitment. Standard Reserved Instances are tied to a specific instance family and Region and do not cover Fargate or Lambda. Spot Instances involve no commitment and can be interrupted. Dedicated Instances are about hardware isolation, not commitment discounts.

prompt: Which Amazon EC2 pricing options provide a discount in exchange for a 1-year or 3-year commitment? (Choose two.)
explanation: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans both lower the price in return for a 1-year or 3-year commitment. On-Demand Instances have no commitment and no discount. Spot Instances are discounted because they can be interrupted, not because of a commitment. On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve capacity at On-Demand rates without a term commitment or a discount.

prompt: A company uploads large amounts of data from its offices to Amazon S3 and later serves some of that data to users on the internet. How does AWS generally charge for this data transfer?

options.text: Both inbound and outbound transfer are charged at the same rate
Inbound transfer is charged; outbound transfer to the internet is free
Inbound transfer from the internet is free; outbound transfer to the internet is charged

explanation: In general, AWS does not charge for data transferred in from the internet, and charges for data transferred out to the internet. That rules out equal charges in both directions and free outbound transfer. Data transfer is not free in every direction, so outbound usage should be part of any cost estimate.

prompt: A company must use existing software licenses that are tied to physical servers, such as per-socket licenses. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option supports this?
explanation: Dedicated Hosts give you a physical server and visibility into its sockets and cores, so you can use server-bound licenses. Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware but without host-level visibility. Spot Instances are discounted spare capacity. Savings Plans are a pricing commitment, not a hardware choice.

prompt: A company stores data in Amazon S3 but does not know how often it will be accessed, and the pattern may change. Which storage class optimizes cost automatically?
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers automatically based on how they are used, which suits unknown or changing access patterns. Standard-IA and One Zone-IA suit data you know is accessed infrequently. Glacier Deep Archive suits long-term archives with retrieval in hours.

prompt: A finance team wants to be notified when the month's actual or forecasted AWS spend passes a threshold the team defines. Which tool should the team use?
explanation: AWS Budgets lets you set custom cost or usage budgets and sends alerts when actual or forecasted amounts exceed your thresholds. Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes past and forecasted spend but is not the alerting tool. Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of resources before you use them. The Cost and Usage Report delivers detailed billing data for analysis.

prompt: An architect wants to estimate the monthly cost of a planned architecture before creating any resources. Which tool should the architect use?
explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator creates cost estimates for planned AWS usage before anything is deployed. AWS Budgets tracks spend against thresholds for an existing account. Cost Explorer analyzes costs that have already been incurred and forecasts from that history. Billing Conductor customizes how billing data is presented, for example for showback and chargeback.

prompt: What is a benefit of consolidated billing in AWS Organizations?

options.text: Each member account receives its own separate AWS Free Tier allowance
Usage across accounts is combined, which can qualify the organization for volume pricing discounts
Data transfer between member accounts is no longer charged
Member accounts no longer need IAM policies

explanation: Consolidated billing gives one bill for all accounts and combines their usage, so the organization can reach volume pricing tiers and share commitment discounts. The Free Tier is applied to the organization as a whole, not once per account. Data transfer is still charged according to normal pricing. Billing consolidation has nothing to do with IAM policies, which are still required.

prompt: A company wants its cost reports to show spending broken down by project and department. What should the company use to categorize its resources?
explanation: After you activate cost allocation tags, AWS uses the tags on your resources to organize costs in cost reports, for example by project or department. IAM groups organize users for permissions. Security groups control network traffic. Availability Zones are locations for resources and say nothing about which project owns a cost.

prompt: A finance team wants to explore the company's AWS costs over the past months, broken down by service, and see a forecast. Which tool should it use?
explanation: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes historical costs and usage, with filtering by service and forecasts. AWS Budgets alerts when spending passes thresholds. Pricing Calculator estimates costs before deployment. Billing Conductor customizes billing data for showback and chargeback.

prompt: Which tool inspects an AWS environment and gives recommendations in categories such as cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits?
explanation: Trusted Advisor checks your account against best practices and makes recommendations across categories including cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits. The Health Dashboard reports AWS service events and how they affect your resources. Amazon Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities only. AWS Artifact provides compliance reports.

prompt: Which statements about AWS Marketplace are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: It is a curated digital catalog for finding, buying, and deploying third-party software
It lists only software that is built by AWS
It is where customers download AWS SOC reports
Charges for purchases appear on the customer's AWS bill
It sends alerts about AWS service events that affect an account

explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated digital catalog of software, data, and services from independent vendors, and purchases are charged through the customer's AWS bill. It is not limited to AWS-built software; most listings come from third parties. SOC reports are downloaded from AWS Artifact. Alerts about service events come from the AWS Health Dashboard.

prompt: Which AWS resource notifies customers about AWS service events, such as scheduled maintenance, that may affect their own resources?
explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard shows events from AWS that can affect your account and resources, such as scheduled maintenance and service issues; the AWS Health API provides the same programmatically. Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations. CloudTrail records API activity. Cost Explorer analyzes costs.

prompt: A company wants a team of AWS experts to help plan and carry out a large migration project. Which AWS offering provides this?
explanation: AWS Professional Services is a global team of experts that works with customers on projects such as migrations. Trusted Advisor is an automated recommendation tool. AWS Artifact provides compliance reports. Basic Support covers account and billing questions and documentation, not project work.

prompt: Which AWS program brings together consulting firms, system integrators, and independent software vendors (ISVs) that help customers build solutions on AWS?
explanation: The AWS Partner Network is the global community of partners, including consulting partners, system integrators, and ISVs. AWS Activate supports startups with credits and resources. AWS Marketplace is the catalog where partner software is sold. AWS Managed Services operates infrastructure on a customer's behalf.
